bifrost: none (no force-feedback device layer; evdev reader in springboard/src/bare/input.rs ignores EV_FF)
summary: Apple's Force Feedback framework is a legacy C API (FFCreateDevice, FFEffectDownload, FFEffectStart) for HID force-feedback devices such as wheels and joysticks. BifrOSt has no force-feedback code path: the evdev reader does not read EV_FF capabilities or upload effects, and the SDK's haptic() call is dropped by the shell. Nothing in the framework is covered.

features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 2 (theme-27, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. evdev bitmaps are parsed for keys, abs and switches only; no check for the FF capability bit, so a wheel or gamepad with force feedback is not identified as one

features.apple: FFDeviceCreateEffect, FFEffectDownload, FFEffectStart, FFEffectStop, FFEffectUnload, FFEffectSetParameters, FFEffectGetParameters, FFEFFECT, FFPERIODIC, FFCONSTANTFORCE, FFRAMPFORCE, FFCONDITION, FFCUSTOMFORCE, FFENVELOPE

features.apple: FFDeviceGetForceFeedbackProperty, FFDeviceSetForceFeedbackProperty, FFDeviceGetForceFeedbackState, FFDeviceSendForceFeedbackCommand, FFState, FFProperty

Apple's own API marks FFDeviceSetCooperativeLevel as unimplemented in version 1.0; nothing to match

features.apple: ForceFeedback.h public interfaces, kFFAPI version variables, FFDeviceObjectReference, FFEffectObjectReference
features.note: Apple's plug-in model sits on IOKit/HID Manager, a macOS driver stack. On Linux the kernel evdev layer provides the equivalent, and BifrOSt does not expose it to apps, so the row is only a gap if app-facing FF is wanted

features.apple: No direct Force Feedback counterpart; closest is a generic haptic call
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:258 (haptic() sends ToShell::Haptic); springboard/proto/src/lib.rs:599 (ToShell::Haptic); springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs:1184 (default arm drops it)
features.note: the SDK call is a no-op: the shell's message match has no Haptic arm
a Settings switch only shown when a sysfs vibrator node exists; it does not drive any force-feedback device or effect

gaps: No evdev force-feedback path: EV_FF is not read, no EVIOCSFF effect upload, no play events (springboard/src/bare/input.rs has no EV_FF; grep count 0).
No device-level FF discovery or capability query for wheels and joysticks (springboard/src/bare/input.rs:299 parses bitmaps but not the FF bit).
No SDK API for effects (constant, periodic, ramp, spring and friction) or for gain and autocenter properties.
The SDK haptic() call is dropped by the shell (springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs:1184 default arm); there is no feedback path from an app to a device.

Web gamepad input is compiled into the browser engine (springboard/apps/browser/engine/Cargo.toml:13, feature gamepad). Whether vibration actuators reach a device was not verified, and this is not covered by this framework row.
The MCP uinput virtual keyboard (springboard/mcp/src/keys.rs:28) sets ff_effects_max in its setup struct for the agent keyboard only; it does not create or drive a force-feedback device.
